label: bidriware/chemistry/why-copper
title: What does the copper do?
description: A choice between two answers to the question what does the copper do, each from the sources on bidri.

u0003.text: One artisan adds 60 gm of copper to every kilogram of zinc to get the perfect black hue.

u0005.text: Quality marking asks for 93% to 94% zinc and 6% to 7% copper in the base alloy.

C080.text: One bidri artisan told The News Minute that 60 gm of copper goes into every kilogram of zinc to get the perfect black hue.

quotes.quote: For every kilogram of zinc, we use 60 gm of copper for it to get the perfect black hue.

C089.text: The census monograph reproduces quality-marking standards set for Bidriware at Hyderabad, requiring a base alloy of 93% to 94% zinc and 6% to 7% copper and inlay silver of at least 96%.

quotes.quote: a quality marking scheme was introduced in the State first on a voluntary basis in 1960
The scheme was extended by phases to the other crafts also, including Bidriware at Hyderabad.
Those set up for Bidriware are reproduced below: 1. Base alloy should have the following com position: Zinc = 93% to 94% Copper = 6% to 7%
Silver used for inlay work shOUld contain a minimum of 96% silver
